strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds the first bounded runtime-owned progress model to existing run.inspect and task.inspect responses.
Lets headless callers decide the next explicit action without reimplementing progress inference from fragmented inspection fields or raw ledgers.
Derives progress from persisted task records and summary-only ledger evidence while avoiding new ledger writes during inspection.
Keeps progress classification inside the Rust runtime and leaves the VSIX as a strict protocol validator, not a policy owner.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances progress_visualization directly, with support for headless_autonomous_development, persistent_structured_ledger, and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: Existing run.inspect and task.inspect now return run.progress_snapshot with lifecycle phase, current stage, next action, bounded evidence counts, and a replay-safe source fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing inspection fields expose fragmented task, child, verifier, recovery, apply, index, and timeline details. Callers must currently infer progress outside the runtime.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless callers and future VSIX progress UI would keep scraping inspection fragments and duplicating runtime-specific progress inference.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M9.4 selected index handles, M9.5 read selected files, and M9.6 materialized selected context into task.run prompts. None classified active task/run progress.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This phase reuses run.inspect and task.inspect and adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: No. A single bounded progress_snapshot is the capability because the runtime needs to own progress classification; it is not a report/digest/history wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime computes deterministic progress classification and next action from TaskRecord status, child task records, and sanitized ledger evidence on inspection.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can inspect one task or run and receive a stable next action without scanning raw ledger events or reproducing milestone-specific logic.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the M10 foundation for progress visualization by defining the first runtime-owned progress contract.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M10.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm runtime-owned progress classification on existing inspection responses, not a wrapper or new endpoint.

exit_criteria: Existing task.inspect returns the same snapshot under run.progress_snapshot
Snapshot lifecycle and stage are derived from runtime task status and ledger evidence, not caller-supplied fields
Created, running, terminal, child-pending, failed-verification, and selected-index-context cases have behavior tests
Controlled child pending, terminal, and non-runnable counts influence bounded next_action guidance
Failed verification evidence produces start_verification_recovery_explicitly guidance when derivable
Selected-index prompt context is represented only as bounded signal presence/count and never raw content or path
Snapshot includes a SHA-256 source_fingerprint over bounded source state
VSIX validators accept valid snapshots and reject invalid enum values and raw fields
No new JSON-RPC method, diagnostics wrapper, report, digest, history, readiness, preview, execution, mutation, shell/git/network/service action, or VSIX policy inference is added
